findings.message: One direct quote drops a word and truncates without an ellipsis
findings.details: Article quotes the PEG-parser post as saying: "Python switched from its LL(1) parser to a PEG-based parser in Python 3.9, also motivated by additional flexibility." The snapshot (source-1.html.gz) actually reads: "Python switched from its LL(1) parser to a PEG-based parser in Python 3.9, also motivated by the additional flexibility PEG provides to evolve the language." The article's quoted span omits the word "the" before "additional" and silently truncates the trailing clause ("PEG provides to evolve the language") without an ellipsis. The substance is not misrepresented, but the text inside quote marks is not verbatim. Filed as a corrections record; see src/content/corrections/2026-08/20-duckdb-previews-v20-cyanoptera-replacing-its-postgres-derived-parser-with-a-peg-grammar-ahead-of-a-fall-release.json.

## Overview

The preview post, written by DuckDB Labs co-founders Mark Raasveldt and Hannes Mühleisen, says ["DuckDB v2.0 is coming this fall"](https://duckdb.org/2026/08/17/duckdb-20-highlights.html) and outlines a set of headline changes that include a clien...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized News piece (1,180 words, within the 400-1200 range) that separates the two source posts cleanly: 'Why the Parser Is Being Replaced' and 'A Parsing Bug Fixed With Memoization' draw from the PEG-parser deep dive, while 'The Rest of the v2.0 Preview' draws from the highlights post. The 'What We Don't Know' section appropriately flags that the release date is only 'this fall' and that several pieces (including the runtime grammar-extension API) are previews subject to change. Technical explanations of PEG vs. YACC/Bison, packrat parsing/memoization, and the parser-vs-binder distinction are accurate paraphrases of the source material.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 sources read from local snapshots (not re-fetched): source-0.html.gz (duckdb.org/2026/08/17/duckdb-20-highlights.html, sha256 verified against manifest), source-1.html.gz (duckdb.org/2026/08/20/duckdb-20-peg-parser.html, sha256 verified), source-2.html.gz (github.com/duckdb/duckdb/releases, sha256 verified). All three returned HTTP 200, none used archive_fallback, and manifest.json shows suspicious_patterns: null for every entry (confirmed by inspecting the manifest directly, not just the summary). source-0 confirms the 'Cyanoptera' codename, the fall-2026 timeline, the client/server ('Quack'/CONNECT) mode, triggers, the storage-format bump to v2.0.0, the ICU removal, the C API revamp, and the '10,000 commits since v1.5' figure -- all quotes checked verbatim and matched except one (see Quote Fidelity finding). source-1 confirms the PEG-vs-YACC/Bison rationale, the 2018 first-commit lineage, the Python 3.9 PEG comparison, the parser/transformer/binder pipeline description, both example-query error messages (Parser Error and Catalog Error, checked character-for-character), the parenthesis-benchmark timings (5.303s / 10.640s / 0.001s), and the pipe-syntax extension demo -- all quotes verbatim except the Python 3.9 one flagged above. source-2 (GitHub releases) confirms v1.5.5 is the 'Latest' tagged release, dated 2026-07-22T10:52:48Z (article rounds to 'July 22, 2026'), and that no v2.0 tag exists in the release list, supporting the article's 'no v2.0 tag yet ... consistent with the fall timeline' framing.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specific claims, numbers, error messages, and code examples trace to the two DuckDB blog posts. One quote (the Python 3.9 PEG comparison) is not verbatim -- it drops the word 'the' and truncates the trailing clause without an ellipsis; substance is preserved but the exact wording inside quote marks does not match the source. This is the sole factual-accuracy issue found and is addressed with a corrections record. No fabricated specifics, no orphan source URLs (all three cited sources also appear in article.sources), no hallucinated quotes beyond the one flagged.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual throughout. No editorializing about whether the parser rewrite or client/server pivot is a good idea; claims about performance (e.g., the 40x recursive-query speedup) are consistently attributed to the DuckDB team's own benchmarking rather than presented as independently verified.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate. The Machine Herald's only prior DuckDB coverage is src/content/articles/2026-04/04-duckdb-150-ships-variant-type-built-in-geometry-and-overhauled-cli-in-largest-release-since-10.md (DuckDB 1.5.0, published April 2026), which explicitly flagged 'the planned DuckDB 2.0 milestone... currently slated for September 2026' as forthcoming (confirmed by grep of that article's body). This submission is a genuine, distinct follow-up covering the actual v2.0 preview content (parser rewrite, client/server mode, triggers, etc.) that did not exist at the time of the 1.5.0 article. No other article in src/content/articles/ references DuckDB.
editor_notes.source_allowlist: duckdb.org was not on config/source_allowlist.txt at submission time. Judged on its own merits: it is DuckDB's own official first-party engineering blog, authored by named DuckDB Labs personnel (co-founders Mark Raasveldt and Hannes Mühleisen on the highlights post; engineer Daniel ten Wolde on the parser deep dive), and is the primary source for the project's own release announcements -- the same tier as already-listed official vendor/project blogs (clickhouse.com, turso.tech, openproject.org, zed.dev). All quotes attributed to it were verified verbatim against the snapshots (aside from the one flagged truncation) during this review. Adding duckdb.org to config/source_allowlist.txt as part of this review, following the existing batch-addition precedent.
editor_notes.suspicious_patterns: manifest.json shows suspicious_patterns: null for all three sources -- no regex matches to evaluate.
concerns: One direct quote (the Python 3.9 PEG-parser comparison) omits the word 'the' and truncates the source sentence without an ellipsis marker -- addressed via corrections record.
recommendations: Bot should use ellipses when truncating mid-sentence quotes, and should double-check word-for-word fidelity (including small function words like articles) before wrapping text in quote marks.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively strong, well-sourced technical preview article with accurate technical explanations and correct GitHub-releases cross-check. The single quote-fidelity issue is minor, does not affect the headline/summary/lead, and is honestly coverable with one corrections entry. duckdb.org is added to the source allowlist as an official first-party vendor blog per existing precedent. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
